name: Daniel Joseph Houston
current_role: Retired Executive Chair of Principal Financial Group (2025); director of ADT Inc. and Arch Capital Group; co-chair, ICON Water Trail board
profile: Dan Houston joined Bankers Life (later Principal Financial Group) in 1984 straight out of Iowa State, selling the then-new 401(k), and rose to CEO in 2015 and chairman in 2016. He retired in 2025 after a 41-year career and now sits on the ADT and Arch Capital boards while focusing on Des Moines civic projects such as the ICON Water Trail.
interesting_fact: He spent his entire 41-year career at one company, starting as a young recruit hired to sell the brand-new 401(k) product and finishing as chairman and CEO of Principal.
deep_cut_fact: A vintage-car enthusiast, he owns 1961 and 1963 Corvettes and a 1970 Mustang, but his favourite is a 1970 El Camino Super Sport; as a teen he raised pigs on his grandparents' farm near Dow City, Iowa, earning about $5,000 one summer.
notes: Now retired from Principal; best routes are via his board roles or Des Moines civic organisations (ICON Water Trail, Community Foundation of Greater Des Moines). No personal published contact found. Strong fit for an entrepreneurship/infrastructure angle (water trail, public transit).

name: Barry Hytinen
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Iron Mountain Inc.; director, ABM Industries
profile: Barry Hytinen has been CFO of Iron Mountain since January 2020, helping steer the records-storage company's push into data centers. Before that he was CFO of Hanesbrands and spent 12 years at Tempur Sealy (including as CFO), after earlier finance roles at GE, Vignette and venture-backed Fogbreak Software.
interesting_fact: As CFO he is a key financial architect of Iron Mountain's pivot from paper-records storage into a fast-growing data-center business, highly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He is a 1997 political science graduate of Syracuse University's Maxwell School (later Harvard MBA), and early on was VP Finance at Fogbreak Software, a small venture-backed Milpitas software startup.
notes: Fogbreak detail comes from secondary bio aggregators (marketscreener/vectorshift); Syracuse/Harvard and Tempur/Hanes facts are from the Maxwell page. Route via Iron Mountain IR or media team.

name: Julia L. Kaercher
current_role: Executive Director, Merchants Foundation (charitable arm of Merchants Bancorp); director nominee/director, Merchants Bancorp
profile: Julia Kaercher has led Merchants Foundation, the charitable arm of Indiana-based Merchants Bancorp, since 2022 and was nominated to the bank's board in 2026. She was previously VP of Program Development at RDOOR Housing Corp., an Indianapolis affordable-housing non-profit. Her listed wealth reflects Merchants Bancorp shares, partly held as trustee.
interesting_fact: She is a founding board member of both the National Women's Affordable Housing Network and the Indiana Women's Affordable Housing Network.
deep_cut_fact: She earned her degree in sport management at the University of Dayton before building a career in affordable-housing program development.
notes: Not an entrepreneur in her own right; she is the daughter of Merchants Bancorp chairman/CEO Michael Petrie (per proxy) and works in philanthropy/affordable housing. Low public profile; route via Merchants Bancorp / Merchants Foundation. Limited fit for energy/data-center theme.

name: Richard Jacinto II
current_role: Private investor; ~10% holder of DiaMedica Therapeutics (DMAC) via a self-directed Roth IRA
profile: Richard Jacinto II appears in SEC filings as a passive 10%-class shareholder of Minneapolis-based DiaMedica Therapeutics, holding about 4.96 million shares (9.6%) through a Roth IRA as of August 2025, and bought 400,000 units in the company's $30.1M private placement in July 2025. No public biography, company role or media presence could be found.
interesting_fact: He holds his ~9.6% stake in a clinical-stage biotech entirely through a self-directed Roth IRA, and added $1.4M in DiaMedica's July 2025 private placement.
notes: Very private individual investor with no public profile; identity beyond SEC filings could not be confirmed. Not an entrepreneur/energy figure. Only route would be via DiaMedica investor relations; low priority.

name: Joshua J. Ofman
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, GRAIL, Inc. (multi-cancer early detection; Galleri test)
profile: Josh Ofman, MD, MSHS, is CEO of GRAIL, maker of the Galleri multi-cancer early-detection blood test, having joined in 2019 and served as Chief Medical Officer and President. Before GRAIL he spent 15+ years at Amgen, finishing as SVP Global Value, Access and Policy. In 2026 he led Galleri through its FDA premarket review, which won a favourable advisory-panel vote in September.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership an FDA advisory committee voted in September 2026 in favour of approving Galleri, a single blood test designed to screen for many cancers at once.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he trained as a gastroenterologist (Internal Medicine and Digestive Diseases at UCLA) and was on the digestive-diseases faculty at Cedars-Sinai; his undergraduate degree from UC Berkeley was in the history and philosophy of science.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Milken Institute, Personalized Medicine Coalition), so open to public conversation. Route via GRAIL corporate communications (pr@grail.com). Health-tech rather than energy fit.

name: Jason Trevisan
profile: Jason Trevisan has been CEO of CarGurus, the Boston-based online automotive marketplace, since January 2021, after joining in 2015 as CFO and later also serving as President of International. Before CarGurus he spent about 12 years at venture firm Polaris Partners (General Partner from 2010), and earlier worked at aQuantive and Bain & Company.
interesting_fact: He moved from the VC side of the table (General Partner at Polaris Partners) to operating as CFO of CarGurus ahead of its 2017 IPO, then became its CEO.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance and venture capital he earned an A.B. in English at Duke, then worked as a Bain consultant and in analytics/client-services management at digital-ad firm aQuantive (bought by Microsoft in 2007), before his Tuck MBA.
notes: Route via CarGurus PR (pr@cargurus.com). Good entrepreneurship/VC-to-operator angle.

name: Jo Ann Wilks
current_role: Private investor; 10%-plus holder of ProFrac Holding Corp. (via the Wilks family); trustee, The Thirteen Foundation (Cisco, Texas)
profile: Jo Ann Wilks is the wife of Farris Wilks, who with his brother Dan built frac-services company Frac Tech from Wilks Masonry and sold their 70% stake for $3.5B in 2011. The family later created ProFrac Holding Corp., in which she is listed as a 10% owner. She and Farris are trustees of The Thirteen Foundation, a Cisco, Texas family foundation.
interesting_fact: The Wilks fortune began with Wilks Masonry, a bricklaying business founded in 1995 by sons of a Cisco, Texas bricklayer, before pivoting to hydraulic fracturing with Frac Tech in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 she and Farris each contributed $50 million to found The Thirteen Foundation, a family foundation that mainly funds causes in Texas and on which both serve as unpaid trustees.
notes: Very private; no public statements or personal channels. Wealth and public role are tied to husband Farris Wilks and the Wilks family's ProFrac stake. The family's philanthropy/political giving is politically sensitive; approach via ProFrac (energy/fracking angle) if at all. The $50M figure comes from DeSmog; ProPublica confirms the trustee roles.

name: James V Continenza
current_role: Executive Chairman (since Feb 2019) and Chief Executive Officer (since July 2020), Eastman Kodak Company
profile: Jim Continenza is a turnaround specialist who joined Kodak's board in 2013, became Executive Chairman in 2019 and CEO in 2020, refocusing the company on print, advanced materials and chemicals. His earlier career was in telecom: AT&T, Lucent Technologies Product Finance, Teligent and STi Prepaid, and he has chaired marketing-tech firm Vivial since 2012.
interesting_fact: He has made a career of steering companies through restructurings, from telecom names like Teligent to Anchor Glass Container (interim CEO, 2006), before taking the helm of the 140-year-old Kodak brand.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career at AT&T, where he worked until 1997, and he holds a liberal arts bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin.
notes: Kodak press releases list individual media staff emails that vary by release; check the latest release for the current media contact. Kodak's advanced materials/battery-component work could be an energy angle.

name: Patrick Wendell
current_role: Co-founder, Databricks; leads the company's AI efforts (Genie, Unity Gateway, model-provider partnerships)
profile: Patrick Wendell is one of the UC Berkeley AMPLab researchers behind Apache Spark who co-founded Databricks in 2013, now one of the world's most valuable private data/AI companies. Long its VP of Engineering, he now leads Databricks' AI efforts, including Genie, Unity Gateway and partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
interesting_fact: He was a founding committer and PMC member of Apache Spark and served as release manager for several Spark releases, including Spark 1.0.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated summa cum laude with a B.S.E. in computer science from Princeton, and his Berkeley M.S. research focused on optimizing large-scale analytics workloads; in 2022 he returned to Princeton to talk founding Databricks with CS chair Jen Rexford.
notes: Low public profile compared with co-founders Ghodsi/Zaharia; strong AI/data-center infrastructure fit. Route via Databricks press team. Spark 1.0 release-manager detail is from the Princeton alumni event page; Rexford event from same page.
